subject.title: [Bug] Agent context window fragmentation during concurrent subagent tool calls

question: Should concurrent subagent results remain completion-ordered push events, or should OpenClaw add an explicit ordered fan-in contract for a requester-defined batch?
rationale: Spawn-order delivery trades responsiveness for deterministic aggregation and requires policy for slow, failed, cancelled, and never-completing earlier children; current documentation establishes completion-order push behavior but does not define ordered batches.

options.title: Keep completion order
options.body: Preserve current non-blocking delivery and require a concrete transcript showing incorrect child correlation before changing runtime behavior.

options.title: Add explicit ordered batches
options.body: Design a requester-owned barrier or aggregation primitive with stable child identities, timeout behavior, and partial-failure handling.

options.title: Enforce spawn order globally
options.body: Buffer every concurrent completion behind earlier children, accepting delayed delivery and new failure-blocking behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep completion order
recommendation.body: Preserve current non-blocking delivery and require a concrete transcript showing incorrect child correlation before changing runtime behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The structured completion-event and surrounding delivery history most strongly connects this owner to the existing product contract.
